function: no_learning: model-based LS/grid-search channel estimation (pp. 6-9) and relaxation-based RIS state optimization (pp. 9-10); the only DNN approximates the RIS element response (pp. 5-6).
notes: Title and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2026.3650846 on p. 1 match. The only learned component is a DNN (with a Legendre-kernel regression alternative) that approximates the pixel-RIS element response nu(phi_in, phi_out; l), trained on angle samples with an approximation-NMSE loss: p. 6 "randomly selecting 10^7 pairs of incident and reflection angles for each RIS state" (eq. 20; Table I, p. 7). p. 4: "the RIS response function is determined solely by the structure of the pixel RIS element and is independent of the wireless propagation variables", so the DNN models hardware, not the channel. The physical-layer functions are not learned: Section IV is "Model-Based Channel Estimation" (p. 6), p. 8 "estimated by the least squares (LS) method", with grid searches P(C-1) to P(C-3) (pp. 8-9); the RIS states come from a softmax relaxation optimized per channel instance without training data, p. 10 "We solve P(A-3) by utilizing Adam optimizer [39] in PyTorch". Section VI (pp. 10-11) does not say whether the DNN or the kernel fit is used for Figs. 10-12, and no result isolates a learned contribution to estimation or beamforming. Borderline for the reviewer: if the response surrogate is counted as a learned part of channel prediction for unseen RIS states (p. 2), the work would be included as area 3 (main metric achievable rate, Figs. 11-12, p. 11); if response modelling is taken as a function of its own, code function (metasurface hardware response modelling) applies instead. Either way the channel estimator and the RIS configuration are non-learned.
